Documentation. The server code is byte-for-byte the one shipped in v4.5.3 — no
tool behaves differently, and the server still declares 109.

The bundle carries its own copy of the READMEs, so this release exists to put
the corrected ones in your hands.

## The READMEs stopped at v4.4.0

Four releases had gone by without them. Both the Italian and English versions
now carry a section for each, in the same order as everything before.

## The tool tables described tools that had moved on

Rows for `get_sleep_data`, `get_stress_data`, `get_available_badges`,
`get_earned_badges` and `delete_weigh_in` did not mention the parameters added
in v4.5.0 and v4.5.1, so the summarised responses looked like missing data
rather than a deliberate default with a way to ask for more.

`create_workout` listed sports including `hiking`, which the workout service has
never had. `get_user_profile` did not say which of the two ids it returns is the
one anything else accepts. `update_gear` did not mention that brand and model
share a single label.

## Two entries were wrong rather than out of date

The gear section listed **`update_gear` as working**. It was not: every call
raised an error until v4.5.3, and anyone reading that line would have trusted it.

**`create_gear`** was described as removed *because the API returns 403
Forbidden*. That reading was mistaken. The endpoint is reachable, and the 403
only appears when the wrong profile identifier is sent. What actually prevents
it is an undocumented request format — nine variations, including the one
published by the client library this project is built on, are all rejected
without the service saying which field is at fault. Gear still has to be created
in the Garmin app or website, but now for the real reason.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.3...v4.5.4
